Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure occurs due to the exception being thrown in the method NodePointer.compareNodePointers, which is called during the evaluation of the union XPath expression "$var | /MAIN/A" in the test testUnionOfVariableAndNode.

- The test creates a document with two <A/> elements under <MAIN>, then initializes a JXPathContext on this document.
- It declares a variable "var" with the string "varValue".
- It then attempts to iterate pointers over the XPath expression "$var | /MAIN/A", which is a union of a variable reference and a node set.
- Inside NodePointer.compareNodePointers, pointers are recursively compared by their parents to establish an ordering or equivalence.
- The comparison method expects the two pointers to belong to the same tree hierarchy; when this is not the case (detected at depth 1), it throws the exception: "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree."
- The likely root cause is that union evaluation tries to mix pointers from different contexts: the variable pointer (which points to a variable object, a string here) versus pointers to nodes in the document.
- Because these pointers do not share a common document root or parent chain, their comparison fails.
- Thus, the issue arises when the union expression contains pointers from heterogeneous trees (variable vs DOM nodes), which the pointer comparison code does not handle gracefully.

Next, it would be useful to inspect how JXPathContext.iteratePointers processes union expressions involving variables and nodes, or how pointers are created and compared during union evaluation. This will help to verify if the system assumes pointers in a union must belong to the same tree and lacks safeguards for this case.

Suggested methods for further inspection or fix include:
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String)
- org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.model.NodePointer.compareNodePointers(NodePointer)
- Any method responsible for union evaluation involving variables and node sets.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
